# Theoretical background

<!-- TODO: turn the notes below into prose (~½ page). See PLAN.md §2. -->

**Inverse problem.** We observe $y = x + n$, $n \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2 I)$. Classical denoising solves $\hat{x} = \arg\min_x \lVert x - y \rVert^2 + \lambda R(x)$ with a hand-designed regulariser $R$.

**Deep Image Prior.** DIP replaces $R$ by a generator: $\theta^* = \arg\min_\theta \lVert f_\theta(z) - y \rVert^2$, $\hat{x} = f_{\theta^*}(z)$ [@ulyanov2018dip]. The network can eventually fit the noise as well, so early stopping acts as the regulariser.

**Spectral bias.** Convolutional generators fit low-frequency content before high-frequency content. The upsampling operation is a key source of this bias [@heckel2020structuralbias; @heckel2019deepdecoder].

**Bayesian view.** In the infinite-width limit DIP is a Gaussian process prior. Posterior averaging reduces the need for early stopping [@cheng2019bayesian].

**Stopping without the clean image.** For held-out pixels $M$ that never enter the loss,
$$\mathbb{E}\big[\lVert f_\theta(z) - y \rVert_M^2\big] = \lVert f_\theta(z) - x \rVert_M^2 + |M|\sigma^2,$$
so the held-out loss tracks the true error. The discrepancy principle stops once the training MSE falls below $\sigma^2$.

**Metrics.** PSNR $= 10\log_{10}(1/\text{MSE})$ and SSIM [@wang2004ssim].
